key_points: OpenAI's official launch: most intelligent and aligned model, now in ChatGPT Work, Codex, and API
Positioned around state-of-the-art computer use, a step change in professional work, and cybersecurity crossing the Critical Preparedness threshold
Works in apps without APIs (fills forms, CRM, calendar, research, drafting, QA) from day one in existing workflows
Excel World Championship example: completes Financial Modeling World Cup challenges ~4x faster than the human winner via computer use
Enterprise endorsements: Devin/Cognition, Databricks OfficeQA Pro, Hebbia decks followed brief 17% more faithfully
Flagship succeeding GPT-5.6 Sol, priced $10/$50 per million input/output tokens
OSWorld 2.0 computer use: 72.6% in ~40 min vs Sol's 65.7% in ~75 min (~47% less time)
Saturates FrontierMath Tier 4 (97.6%) and ExploitBench (100%)
ARC-AGI-3 99.9% depends on a stateful, expensive harness; stateless API calls score far lower (17-63%)
Trails Claude Fable 5.1 on Humanity's Last Exam with tools (57.2% vs 65.0%) — not a clean sweep
Crosses Critical cybersecurity threshold; exploit-creation gated behind OpenAI's Daybreak program
Available as gpt-6-astra via OpenAI API, Amazon Bedrock, Azure; GPT-6 Astra Pro tier
Released 3 September 2026, first model above the GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna family
API model ID gpt-6-astra; $10 input / $50 output per M tokens; 1,050,000-token context window
Knowledge cutoff 30 April 2026 (vs 16 Feb 2026 for GPT-5.6 family) — ~10-week gain
Context window is total budget; input capped at 922,000 (chunk against this, not the headline)
272K pricing cliff sits below headline context — key API migration gotcha
Single dense reasoning model, 1M-token class context, five reasoning-effort settings (low/medium/high/xhigh/max); no mini/nano tier
Max input/output 922,000 / 128,000 tokens; text+image in, text out
Strongest deep-context retention published: 3% loss only in 512K-1M band on deep-context recall
Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index: Astra 61.2 vs Sol 60.9, but behind Claude Fable 5.1 and Opus 5
Generational jump real on agentic, computer-use, cyber, math; roughly flat on general intelligence
Limited preview Sept 3, 2026; paid users following day; rolls out ChatGPT Plus/Pro/Business/Enterprise, API, Azure, AWS Bedrock
Delayed after the Hugging Face incident in July 2026 to add more safeguards
2.5x the price of the model it replaces ($50 vs $20 output per M tokens)
Independent neutral-harness ARC-AGI-3 score is 62.7%, vs OpenAI's claimed 99.9% — big harness caveat
Real step change in a narrow band of work; roughly flat elsewhere

stats.fact: OSWorld 2.0 computer use: 72.6% (GPT-6 Astra) vs 65.7% (GPT-5.6 Sol), at ~40 min vs ~75 min per task (~47% less time)
ARC-AGI-3 claimed 99.9% under stateful provider adapter; independent neutral harness scores 62.7% (OpenAI) / 17-63% (DataCamp stateless)
Pricing: $10 / $50 per million input/output tokens; cached input $1/M; cost ~2.5x GPT-5.6 Sol
Context window 1,050,000 tokens; max input 922,000; max output 128,000
Knowledge cutoff 30 April 2026 (vs 16 Feb 2026 for GPT-5.6 family)
Releases 3 September 2026; delayed after July 2026 Hugging Face incident for added safeguards
Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index: Astra 61 (tied with Sol), below Claude Fable 5.1 (66)
Humanity's Last Exam with tools: Astra 57.2% vs Claude Fable 5.1 65.0%
Terminal-Bench 4.0 (agentic coding): 57.9% vs 37.3% for Sol; new high 57.9% at ~9% and 63% lower est. cost per task vs Sol and Claude Fable 5.1

angles: The computer-use era: ASTRA's OSWorld jump is the real headline, not raw general intelligence — agent you can hand tasks vs. one you babysit
The ARC-AGI-3 harness controversy: 99.9% marketing number relies on a stateful provider adapter; neutral harness scores 62.7% — how to read the benchmark honestly
Cost reality check: 2.5x the price of Sol buys a narrow-band capability gain — is it worth it for you?
Cybersecurity double-edged sword: crosses the 'Critical' threshold, exploit-creation gated behind Daybreak — enterprise safety implications
No Astra mini/nano: unlike GPT-5.6 family, Terra/Luna remain the mid/low cost options — portfolio positioning
Devin, Databricks, Hebbia adoption signals for real enterprise work (decks, financial material, codebase understanding)
